Theme

Body, health & movement

nod verb

also nod your head, nod yes, nod assent, shake your head

classical

Plaut. Asin. 784: neque illa ūllī hominī nūtet, nictet, annuat
Liv. 1.12: adnuentibus ac vocantibus suīs ēvādit (Lewis & Short)

annuō (adnuō), annuere, annuī, annūtum

verb, third conjugation

nod to someone; nod yes, give the nod

Other words

  • nūtō, nūtāre, nūtāvī, nūtātum — nod, keep nodding; make a sign with the head

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Plaut. Mil. 207: capite nūtat: nōn placet quod repperit; Plaut. Men. 612b: nūtat, nē loquar

  • abnuō, abnuere, abnuī — refuse with a movement of the head; say no

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Plaut. Capt. 481: ubi cēnāmus? inquam. atque illī abnuont; Nigid. ap. Gell. 10.4 (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • neque illa ūllī hominī nūtet, nictet, annuat

    and she is not to nod, wink or beckon to any manPlaut. Asin. 784

  • eccere autem capite nūtat: nōn placet quod repperit

    but look, he’s shaking his head: he doesn’t like what he’s come up withPlaut. Mil. 207

See also head, nod off, yes, agree, wink.

SourcesLewis & Short: annuo · Lewis & Short: nuto · Lewis & Short: abnuo

Plautus, Asinaria 784; Captivi 481; Menaechmi 612b; Miles gloriosus 207.
